description: Behavioral regulations (identified regulation), explicit attitudes, and social desirability moderate implicit-explicit discrepancies (IEDs) between automatic associations and explicit exercise motives related to health and appearance outcomes in adults

original_title: Falls in the general hospital: association with delirium, advanced age, and specific surgical procedures
replication_title: Falls in A Tertiary Care Hospital—Association With Delirium: A Replication Study
description: Falls in the general hospital are associated with delirium, with a large proportion (96%) of patients who fell displaying evidence of delirium, most of which was undiagnosed

original_title: Oxytocin improves "mind-reading" in humans
replication_title: Does oxytocin affect mind-reading? A replication study
description: Intranasal oxytocin administration (24IU) improves performance on the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET), enhancing the ability to infer others' mental states from the eye region in healthy males

original_title: Effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor agonist MK212 and 2A receptor antagonist MDL100907 on maternal behavior in postpartum female rats
replication_title: Behavioral, pharmacological and neuroanatomical analysis of serotonin 2C receptor agonism on maternal behavior in rats
description: Acute systemic injection of MK212 (a selective 5-HT2C receptor agonist) dose-dependently disrupts active components of rat maternal behavior, particularly pup retrieval

original_title: Oxytocin receptor genetic variation relates to empathy and stress reactivity in humans
replication_title: Revisiting the impact of OXTR rs53576 on empathy: A population-based study and a meta-analysis
description: Individuals with the GG genotype of OXTR rs53576 have higher levels of empathy than those with the A allele, as measured by self-report questionnaire

original_title: The influence of oxytocin on automatic motor simulation
replication_title: Automatic Imitation in Comorbid PTSD & Alcohol Use Disorder and Controls: an RCT of Intranasal Oxytocin
description: A single intranasal oxytocin administration increases automatic imitation of finger movements in healthy undergraduates, as measured by the congruency effect on the imitation-inhibition task

original_title: Genome-wide association study identifies susceptibility loci for polycystic ovary syndrome on chromosome 2p16.3, 2p21 and 9q33.3
replication_title: Replication study of RAD54B and GREB1 polymorphisms and risk of PCOS in Han Chinese
description: RAD54B (rs2930961) and GREB1 (rs12470971, rs11686574, rs6740248) polymorphisms are associated with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in Han Chinese population, as identified by genome-wide association study with P-values < 10^-5

original_title: Challenging behaviours should not be considered as depressive equivalents in individuals with intellectual disability
replication_title: Challenging behaviors should not be considered depressive equivalents in individuals with intellectual disabilities. II. A replication study
description: Challenging behaviors are not depressive equivalents in individuals with intellectual disability — item and factor analysis of the CBCPID showed that core symptoms of depression cluster together while almost all challenging behaviors are unrelated to depression

original_title: Leadership at the front line: Impact of practice leadership management style on staff experience in services for people with intellectual disability and challenging behaviour
replication_title: Impact of practice leadership management style on staff experience in services for people with intellectual disability and challenging behaviour: A further examination and partial replication
description: Practice leadership (PL) style of frontline management is associated with better staff experiences (lower stress, lower burnout, better teamwork) when working with people with intellectual disabilities and challenging behaviour

original_title: HLA-C and killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor genes in idiopathic bronchiectasis
replication_title: Lack of association between KIR and HLA-C type and susceptibility to idiopathic bronchiectasis
description: Homozygosity for HLA-C group type confers increased genetic susceptibility to idiopathic bronchiectasis, with approximately 50% of idiopathic bronchiectasis patients being HLA-C group 1 homozygous compared with 25% of controls

original_title: Polymorphisms in the trace amine receptor 4 (TRAR4) gene on chromosome 6q23.2 are associated with susceptibility to schizophrenia
replication_title: No association of haplotype-tagging SNPs in TRAR4 with schizophrenia in Japanese patients
description: SNPs in the TRAR4 gene on chromosome 6q23.2 are associated with susceptibility to schizophrenia in European and African American populations

original_title: Emotional processing in schizophrenia across cultures: standardized measures of discrimination and experience
replication_title: Emotional face processing deficit in schizophrenia: A replication study in a South African Xhosa population
description: Schizophrenia patients in American, German, and Indian samples show a selective deficit in recognition of negative facial expressions (particularly anger) while performing normally on positive expressions (happy faces)

original_title: Hearing impairment and psychosis revisited
replication_title: Hearing impairment and psychosis: A replication in a cohort of young adults
description: Individuals with hearing impairment in the past 12 months had a threefold increased risk to develop positive psychotic experiences in a general population sample aged 18-64

original_title: GAD1 (2q31.1), which encodes glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD67), is associated with childhood-onset schizophrenia and cortical gray matter volume loss
replication_title: No association between the glutamate decarboxylase 67 gene (GAD1) and schizophrenia in the Japanese population
description: SNPs in the 5' region of GAD1 (particularly Markers 4 and 5) are associated with childhood-onset schizophrenia and cortical gray matter volume loss

original_title: GAD1, which encodes glutamate decarboxylase 1 (GAD67), is associated with adult onset schizophrenia in two independent samples
replication_title: No association between the glutamate decarboxylase 67 gene (GAD1) and schizophrenia in the Japanese population
description: GAD1 is associated with adult onset schizophrenia in two independent samples

original_title: The association between high nicotine dependence and severe mental illness may be consistent across countries
replication_title: Smoking initiation and schizophrenia: A replication study in a Chinese Han population
description: Schizophrenic patients have a higher rate of ever smoking daily and initiate daily smoking at higher rates after age 20 compared to controls, as shown by survival analysis of age of smoking onset

original_title: Smoking initiation and schizophrenia: a replication study in a Spanish sample
replication_title: Smoking initiation and schizophrenia: A replication study in a Chinese Han population
description: Schizophrenic patients in Spain have higher rates of smoking initiation and initiate daily smoking at higher rates after age 20 compared to controls, as shown by survival analysis of age of smoking onset

original_title: The association between schizophrenia and smoking: unexplained by either the illness or the prodromal period
replication_title: Smoking initiation and schizophrenia: A replication study in a Chinese Han population
description: The association between schizophrenia and smoking initiation rates (higher after age 20) cannot be explained by the illness itself or the prodromal period, as demonstrated by excluding patients who started smoking within 5 years of illness onset

original_title: Effect of schizophrenia on frontotemporal activity during word encoding and recognition: a PET cerebral blood flow study
replication_title: Multimodal analysis of the hippocampus in schizophrenia using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy and functional magnetic resonance imaging
description: Individuals with schizophrenia show an altered (negative) relationship between inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) BOLD response during a memory task and task performance (discriminability), unlike healthy controls who show a positive relationship

original_title: Abnormalities in the establishment of feeling of agency in schizophrenia
replication_title: Abnormalities in the experience of self-agency in schizophrenia: A replication study
description: Schizophrenia patients show impaired prime-based agency inferences (where briefly primed outcome information fails to enhance the sense of self-agency) compared to healthy controls, while both groups show intact goal-based agency inferences

original_title: Social cognition psychometric evaluation: results of the initial psychometric study
replication_title: Psychometrics of social cognitive measures for psychosis treatment research
description: Several social cognitive measures (BLERT, Hinting, TASIT, Eyes, AIHQ) have specific psychometric properties (test-retest reliability, utility as repeated measures, relationship to functioning) suitable for use in schizophrenia clinical trials

original_title: Decreased spectral entropy modulation in patients with schizophrenia during a P300 task
replication_title: Deficit of entropy modulation of the EEG in schizophrenia associated to cognitive performance and symptoms. A replication study
description: Schizophrenia patients show a significantly lower spectral entropy (SE) decrease compared to healthy controls over central-posterior regions during a P300 auditory oddball paradigm, and this deficit is related to positive and total PANSS symptoms

original_title: Antiherpes virus-specific treatment and cognition in schizophrenia: a test-of-concept randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial
replication_title: Herpes simplex virus 1 infection and valacyclovir treatment in schizophrenia: Results from the VISTA study
description: Valacyclovir treatment (compared to placebo) improves working memory and visual learning in HSV-1 seropositive individuals with schizophrenia

original_title: Apathy is associated with ventral striatum volume in schizophrenia spectrum disorder
replication_title: Apathy is not associated with reduced ventral striatal volume in patients with schizophrenia
description: Apathy is associated with reduced right ventral striatum volume in schizophrenia spectrum disorder, as measured by voxel-based morphometry

original_title: Amotivation is associated with smaller ventral striatum volumes in older patients with schizophrenia
replication_title: Apathy is not associated with reduced ventral striatal volume in patients with schizophrenia
description: Amotivation/apathy is associated with reduced bilateral ventral striatum volume in schizophrenia, as measured by the MAGeT-Brain automated segmentation algorithm

original_title: Cognitive performance, symptom severity, and survival among patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders: a prospective 15-year study
replication_title: Neurocognitive function and mortality in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
description: Baseline verbal memory and executive function are particularly strong predictors of survival status in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders approximately 15 years later

original_title: Frontal absences in children
replication_title: Frontal-onset absences in children: Associated with worse outcome? A replication study
description: Children with absence epilepsy who show frontal onset of generalized ictal EEG discharges have worse outcomes, including more difficult-to-treat seizures and more learning and behavioural problems, compared to children with classical generalized onset absences

original_title: Relationships between school start time, sleep duration, and adolescent behaviors
replication_title: Relationships between sleep duration and adolescent depression: a conceptual replication
description: Greater sleep duration and later wake-up times are associated with fewer indicators of depressive mood among high school students

original_title: Structural stigma and all-cause mortality in sexual minority populations
replication_title: Is structural stigma's effect on the mortality of sexual minorities robust? A failure to replicate the results of a published study
description: Sexual minorities residing in communities with high levels of anti-gay prejudice (structural stigma) experience approximately 12 years shorter life expectancy, with a hazard ratio of 3.03 for all-cause mortality compared to sexual minorities in lower-stigma communities

original_title: Relation between 20-year income volatility and brain health in midlife: The CARDIA study
replication_title: 20-Year income volatility and cognitive function in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (1979) cohort: A replication and extension of CARDIA findings
description: Higher income volatility and more substantial income drops over a 20-year period in early-to-mid adulthood are associated with poorer cognitive function in midlife

original_title: Using SHRP 2 naturalistic driving data to assess drivers' speed choice while being engaged in different secondary tasks
replication_title: Do drivers reduce their speed when texting on highways? A replication study using European naturalistic driving data
description: Drivers on free-flow interstates show only a small speed reduction when texting while driving, as analyzed using SHRP 2 naturalistic driving data

original_title: Sleep restriction leads to increased activation of brain regions sensitive to food stimuli
replication_title: Chronic Mild Sleep Restriction Does Not Lead to Marked Neuronal Alterations Compared With Maintained Adequate Sleep in Adults
description: Sleep restriction (4-hour time in bed) leads to increased activation in the insula, nucleus accumbens, and superior frontal gyrus in response to food stimuli compared with nonfood stimuli, relative to adequate sleep

original_title: Sleep restriction increases the neuronal response to unhealthy food in normal-weight individuals
replication_title: Chronic Mild Sleep Restriction Does Not Lead to Marked Neuronal Alterations Compared With Maintained Adequate Sleep in Adults
description: Sleep restriction leads to increased neuronal activation in response to unhealthy food relative to healthy food stimuli, specifically in the inferior, middle, and superior frontal gyrus and inferior parietal gyrus

replication_title: EFFECT OF BORDERLINE PERSONALITY TRAITS ON ANTIDEPRESSANT RESPONSE TO TMS: A REPLICATION ATTEMPT
description: BPD traits do not reduce responsiveness to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) as an antidepressant treatment in patients with major depressive disorder

original_title: Searching for hidden costs: a technology-based approach to the energy efficiency gap in light-duty vehicles
replication_title: Re-searching for hidden costs: Evidence from the adoption of fuel-saving technologies in light-duty vehicles
description: Fuel-saving technologies adopted in light-duty vehicles do not impose hidden costs on operational characteristics such as acceleration, handling, ride comfort, noise, braking feel, and vibration, as evaluated through content analysis of professional auto reviews

original_title: Developing a new generic health and wellbeing measure: psychometric survey results for the EQ-HWB
replication_title: Evaluating the Factor Structure of the Preliminary Version of EuroQol Health and Well-Being Instrument in China: A Replication of the Confirmatory Factor Analysis
description: The UK-based bifactor CFA model for the EQ-HWB, when applied to a Chinese online sample, showed poor model fit (CFI=0.907, RMSEA=0.071) even after adjustments to form a Chinese-adjusted model, suggesting the EQ-HWB factor structure lacks cross-cultural comparability in China

original_title: Reorganization of visual processing in macular degeneration
replication_title: Reorganization of visual processing in macular degeneration: Replication and clues about the role of foveal loss
description: Peripheral visual stimuli activate 'foveal' cortex (foveal confluence at occipital pole) in individuals with macular degeneration who have complete loss of foveal input, indicating large-scale reorganization of visual processing

original_title: Feature guidance by negative attentional templates depends on search difficulty
replication_title: Benefits from negative templates in easy and difficult search depend on rapid distractor rejection and enhanced guidance
description: Negative attentional template (color cue) reaction time benefits are larger during a difficult search task than an easy search task, with benefits absent in the easy condition

original_title: Feature guidance by negative attentional templates depends on search difficulty
replication_title: Benefits from negative templates in easy and difficult search depend on rapid distractor rejection and enhanced guidance
description: Negative attentional template (color cue) reaction time benefits are larger during a difficult search task than an easy search task, with benefits absent in the easy condition

original_title: Effects of chronic estradiol treatment on delayed spatial alternation and differential reinforcement of low rates of responding
replication_title: Impact of estrogen receptor alpha and beta agonists on delayed alternation in middle-aged rats
description: Chronic 17β-estradiol treatment impairs performance of ovariectomized female rats on an operant delayed spatial alternation (DSA) task that engages the prefrontal cortex

original_title: Chronic estradiol replacement impairs performance on an operant delayed spatial alternation task in young, middle-aged, and old rats
replication_title: Impact of estrogen receptor alpha and beta agonists on delayed alternation in middle-aged rats
description: Chronic 17β-estradiol treatment impairs performance of ovariectomized young, middle-aged, and old female rats on an operant delayed spatial alternation (DSA) task that engages the prefrontal cortex

original_title: Men's preference for the ovulating female is triggered by subtle face shape differences
replication_title: Do women's faces become more attractive near ovulation?
description: Men prefer faces with shape cues characteristic of the ovulatory (late follicular) phase over faces characteristic of the luteal phase, suggesting detectable facial cues of women's current fecundity

original_title: Common variants near MC4R are associated with fat mass, weight and risk of obesity
replication_title: Association study of MC4R with complex obesity and replication of the rs17782313 association signal
description: A SNP downstream of the MC4R gene (rs17782313) is significantly associated with increased risk of both adult and childhood obesity in a genome-wide association study

original_title: Real-time EEG-defined excitability states determine efficacy of TMS-induced plasticity in human motor cortex
replication_title: Phase matters when there is power: Phasic modulation of corticospinal excitability occurs at high amplitude sensorimotor mu-oscillations
description: TMS delivered at the negative (trough) peak of high-magnitude sensorimotor mu-oscillations generates significantly larger motor evoked potentials (MEPs) than TMS at the positive (peak) peak, demonstrating phase-dependent modulation of corticospinal excitability that is contingent on mu-oscillation power

original_title: Population modeling with machine learning can enhance measures of mental health
replication_title: Population modeling with machine learning can enhance measures of mental health - Open-data replication
description: Prediction of fluid intelligence trait from resting-state fMRI neuroimaging features using random forest regression yields a maximum R² of approximately 0.02–0.04 in a UK Biobank sample of ~9000 participants

original_title: Population modeling with machine learning can enhance measures of mental health
replication_title: Population modeling with machine learning can enhance measures of mental health - Open-data replication
description: Prediction of neuroticism trait from resting-state fMRI neuroimaging features using random forest regression yields near-zero R² in a UK Biobank sample of ~9000 participants

original_title: Stress-related dysfunction of the right inferior frontal cortex in high ruminators: an fNIRS study
replication_title: Insights from a laboratory and naturalistic investigation on stress, rumination and frontal brain functioning in MDD: An fNIRS study
description: The Trier Social Stress Test (TSST) induces rumination in high trait ruminators and leads to reduced cortical activity in the Cognitive Control Network (CCN), which mediates group differences in post-stress rumination and negative affect between high and low trait ruminators

original_title: Salivary cortisol differs with age and sex and shows inverse associations with WHR in Swedish women: a cross-sectional study
replication_title: Effects of gender-affirming hormones on diurnal cortisol concentrations: A prospective study
description: Females show a steeper diurnal cortisol slope (greater decline from morning to bedtime) compared to males in cisgender adults

original_title: A multidimensional scaling analysis of the techniques that physiotherapists use
replication_title: Multidimensional scaling analysis of techniques used by physiotherapists in Southeast Australia: A cross-national replication
description: Physiotherapists in England use techniques in ordered combinations that differentiate the profession into typologies or specialities (respiratory, neurological, and orthopaedic/musculoskeletal), as revealed by multidimensional scaling analysis

original_title: Psychometric properties of four anxiety measures in older adults
replication_title: Assessing older adults with generalized anxiety: a replication and extension
description: Self-report measures of anxiety (PSWQ, STAI, WS, FQ) demonstrate adequate psychometric properties (internal consistency, convergent validity, interrelation of subscales) in older adults with generalized anxiety disorder

original_title: Strategies of thought control in obsessive-compulsive disorder
replication_title: Thought control strategies in obsessive-compulsive disorder: a replication and extension
description: OCD patients use distraction less frequently and worry and punishment strategies more frequently than non-anxious controls when attempting to control intrusive thoughts

original_title: The hierarchical structure and general factor saturation of the Anxiety Sensitivity Index: Evidence and implications
replication_title: Factor structure and stability of the Anxiety Sensitivity Index in a longitudinal study of anxiety disorder patients
description: The Anxiety Sensitivity Index has a hierarchical factor structure with three lower-order factors (physical concerns, mental incapacitation concerns, and social concerns) all loading on a single second-order general factor

original_title: Effects of varied-stimulus exposure training on fear reduction and return of fear
replication_title: Manipulations of exposure-based therapy to reduce return of fear: a replication
description: Exposure to varied phobic stimuli (multiple spiders) leads to better maintenance of treatment gains at follow-up than exposure to a constant (single) spider, reducing return of fear

original_title: Effects of an expanding-spaced versus massed exposure schedule on fear reduction and return of fear
replication_title: Manipulations of exposure-based therapy to reduce return of fear: a replication
description: An expanding-spaced schedule of exposure trials leads to less return of fear and greater generalization of extinction than massed treatment

original_title: Essential fatty acids predict metabolites of serotonin and dopamine in cerebrospinal fluid among healthy control subjects, and early- and late-onset alcoholics
replication_title: A replication study of violent and nonviolent subjects: cerebrospinal fluid metabolites of serotonin and dopamine are predicted by plasma essential fatty acids
description: Higher plasma docosahexaenoic acid concentrations predict lower cerebrospinal fluid 5-HIAA concentrations (negative correlation) among early-onset alcoholics

original_title: Dimensionality of depression in acute schizophrenia: a methodological study using the Bech-Rafaelsen Melancholia Scale (BRMES)
replication_title: Three dimensions of depression in patients with acute psychotic disorders: A replication study
description: Depression symptoms in acutely schizophrenic patients as measured by the Bech-Rafaelsen Melancholia Scale (BRMES) can best be represented by a three-dimensional model comprising retardation, depressive core symptoms, and accessory depressive symptoms, rather than being unidimensional

original_title: Some relations of grammar and lexicon in aphasia
replication_title: Morphosyntactic Processing in German Agrammatism: A Replication and Revision of Von Stockert/Bader (1976)
description: German Broca's aphasics show near-total loss of morphosyntactic abilities (as shown by poor performance on a constituent ordering nonsense-word task) while Wernicke's aphasics retain them, demonstrating a double dissociation between morphosyntax and lexical semantics in agrammatism

original_title: Chromosome 2 sequence of the human malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum
replication_title: Reproducibility in genome sequence annotation: the Plasmodium falciparum chromosome 2 case
description: Genome sequence annotation of the Plasmodium falciparum chromosome 2, characterizing 210 gene sequences including predicted functions, membrane proteins, and unique sequences

original_title: Psychosocial aspects of anonymous donor insemination
replication_title: Differences in the attitudes of couples whose children were conceived through artificial insemination by donor in 1980 and in 1996
description: Couples who conceive children through artificial insemination by donor (AID) strongly prefer absolute anonymity of the donor and secrecy toward the child about the nature of his or her conception

original_title: Dental factors associated with temporomandibular joint sounds
replication_title: An extended replication study of dental factors associated with temporomandibular joint sounds
description: Dental factors (attrition, non-working-side interferences, molar contacts, Angle's class, horizontal jaw mobility) predict the presence of temporomandibular joint sounds in nonpatients

original_title: Single trial analysis of event-related potentials: a comparison between schizophrenics and depressives
replication_title: A replication study on P300 single trial analysis in schizophrenia: confirmation of a reduced number of ‘true positive’ P300 waves
description: Schizophrenics exhibit fewer 'true positive' P300 waves in single trial analysis of event-related potentials compared to healthy controls, with this reduction being the underlying mechanism of the well-known P300 amplitude reduction in schizophrenia

original_title: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder and thyroid function
replication_title: Thyroid function in attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder
description: Higher prevalence of thyroid abnormalities (5.4%) in ADHD children compared to normal controls (<1%)

original_title: Preclinical memory decline in cognitively normal apolipoprotein E-e4 homozygotes
replication_title: Preclinical cognitive decline in late middle-aged asymptomatic apolipoprotein E-e4/4 homozygotes: a replication study
description: Age-related decline in immediate and delayed memory is steeper in apolipoprotein E-e4/4 homozygotes than in e3/4 heterozygotes and e4 noncarriers, as measured by WAIS-R digit span, AVLT total learning, and AVLT trial 5

original_title: Changes in perceptual asymmetry with the menstrual cycle
replication_title: Replication of a premenstrual decrease in right-ear advantage on language-related dichotic listening tests of cerebral laterality
description: Right-ear advantage (REA) on language-related dichotic listening tasks decreases in the premenstrual week relative to the postmenstrual week

original_title: Neuropsychological correlates of menstrual mood changes
replication_title: Replication of a premenstrual decrease in right-ear advantage on language-related dichotic listening tests of cerebral laterality
description: Women show a tendency to recall fewer positive emotional words (lower positive emotional proclivity index) during the premenstrual week

original_title: Motivational properties of frustration: I. Effect on a running response of the addition of frustration to the motivational complex
replication_title: Amsel's Frustration Effect: A Pavlovian Replication With Control for Frequency and Distribution of Rewards
description: Rats run faster in the second runway of a double runway after a non-rewarded trial than after a rewarded trial, reflecting increased arousal (frustration) induced by unexpected reward omission

original_title: Elevated sodium levels in public drinking water as a contributor to elevated blood pressure levels in the community
replication_title: The influence of elevated levels of sodium in drinking water on elementary and high school students in Massachusetts
description: Tenth grade students from a community with elevated sodium levels (107 mg/L) in drinking water had significantly higher blood pressure distributions than students from a community with low sodium levels (8 mg/L)

original_title: A simple method to measure baseline occupancy of neostriatal dopamine D2 receptors by dopamine in vivo in healthy subjects
replication_title: Effects of catecholamine depletion on D2 receptor binding, mood, and attentiveness in humans: a replication study
description: Catecholamine depletion via AMPT increases neostriatal D2 receptor binding potential and decreases mood and attentiveness in healthy subjects, with attentiveness decrease correlated with D2RBP increase

original_title: Emotional regulation of interactions between two-month-olds and their mothers
replication_title: Infants' sensitivity to interpersonal contingency: An attempt to replicate murray and trevarthen
description: Eight-week-old infants show differential responding to on-line (live) versus deferred (tape) video presentation of their mother in a face-to-face interaction, demonstrating sensitivity to interpersonal contingency

original_title: MRI-based evaluation of locus and extent of neurotoxic lesions in monkeys
replication_title: Assessment of locus and extent of neurotoxic lesions in monkeys using neuroimaging techniques: a replication
description: In vivo neuroimaging techniques (FLAIR and T1-weighted MRI) can accurately quantify the locus and extent of neuronal damage produced by ibotenic acid injections in non-human primates, with neuroimaging estimates correlating highly with histological cell loss

original_title: Suicide in twins
replication_title: Suicidal behavior in twins: a replication
description: Monozygotic twins show significantly greater concordance for completed suicide than dizygotic twins, consistent with a genetic contribution to suicidal behavior

original_title: Attempted suicide among living co-twins of twin suicide victims
replication_title: Suicidal behavior in twins: a replication
description: Monozygotic co-twins of suicide victims show significantly greater rates of attempted suicide than dizygotic co-twins, consistent with a genetic contribution to suicidal behavior

original_title: Lithium response and genetics of affective disorders
replication_title: Autosomal recessive inheritance of affective disorders in families of responders to lithium prophylaxis?
description: Autosomal recessive inheritance is the best-fitting single-gene model for affective disorders in families of lithium-responsive patients, with a relatively common predisposing allele and sex-specific penetrance

original_title: TPQ in euthymic manic depressive patients
replication_title: Low persistence in euthymic manic-depressive patients: a replication
description: Euthymic bipolar patients in a public hospital clinic score significantly lower on the Persistence scale of the Tridimensional Personality Questionnaire (TPQ) compared to US norms, suggesting low Persistence may be a temperament marker for manic-depressive illness

original_title: Syndromes of schizotypy and timing of puberty
replication_title: Timing of puberty and syndromes of schizotypy: a replication☆
description: Extreme early and late maturers at puberty show elevated schizotypy scores (particularly Unreality syndrome in both extremes and Withdrawn syndrome in late maturing males) compared to average maturers in healthy adults

original_title: Association analysis of the 5-HT 6 receptor polymorphism C267T in Alzheimer's disease
replication_title: Association study of the 5-hydroxytryptamine6 receptor gene in Alzheimer's disease
description: The 267C allele of the 5-HT6 receptor gene (267 C/T polymorphism) is associated with increased risk for Alzheimer's disease in a Chinese ethnic population

original_title: The gene encoding nicastrin, a major gamma-secretase component, modifies risk for familial early-onset Alzheimer disease in a Dutch population-based sample
replication_title: No replication of the association between the Nicastrin gene and familial early-onset Alzheimer's disease
description: NCSTN haplotype B increases risk for familial early-onset Alzheimer's disease approximately four-fold in patients without the APOE ε4 allele

original_title: Informed consent in Dutch dental practice: knowledge, attitudes and self-efficacy of dentists
replication_title: Dutch dentists’ views of informed consent: a replication study
description: Dutch dentists have problems with informed consent implementation: they have limited knowledge, somewhat negative attitudes, and low self-efficacy regarding informing patients about treatment

original_title: Predictors of occult blood screening in the elderly
replication_title: Predictors of fecal occult blood screening among older socioeconomically disadvantaged Americans: a replication study
description: Female gender, ability to use the telephone, ability to shop, ability to clean house, and previous FOBT screening are predictors of participation in fecal occult blood testing among socioeconomically disadvantaged elderly populations

original_title: Naltrexone in young autistic children: a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study
replication_title: Naltrexone in Young Autistic Children: Replication Study and Learning Measures
description: Naltrexone (1.0 mg/kg daily) reduces restlessness and hyperactivity in young autistic children and benefits behavior in the majority of children across home, school, and clinical settings in a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design

original_title: Psychotherapists' perspectives on treating themselves and their clients for psychic distress
replication_title: Treating ourselves vs. Treating our clients: A replication with alcohol abuse
description: Psychotherapists' treatment of clients for psychological distress varies as a function of theoretical orientation, whereas their self-change efforts do not, and therapists differ in the change processes they recommend for clients versus themselves

original_title: Association between the a1A-calcium channel gene CACNA1A and idiopathic generalized epilepsy
replication_title: Failure to replicate an allelic association between an exon 8 polymorphism of the human α1A calcium channel gene and common syndromes of idiopathic generalized epilepsy
description: A single nucleotide polymorphism in exon 8 (SNP8) of the CACNA1A gene is associated with common subtypes of idiopathic generalized epilepsy, with the SNP8 A-allele significantly increased in IGE probands compared to controls (OR=1.8) and preferentially transmitted from heterozygous parents to affected offspring

original_title: Genome scan of idiopathic generalized epilepsy: evidence for major susceptibility gene and modifying genes influencing the seizure type
replication_title: No evidence for a susceptibility locus for idiopathic generalized epilepsy on chromosome 5 in families with typical absence seizures
description: Genome-wide scan reveals two susceptibility loci for idiopathic generalized epilepsy on chromosome 5 (regions 5p15 and 5q14-q22) in families with typical absence seizures

original_title: Schizophrenia and smoking: an epidemiological survey in a state hospital
replication_title: Schizophrenia and tobacco smoking: a replication study in another US psychiatric hospital
description: Schizophrenia is associated with a higher rate of current tobacco smoking compared with other severe mental illnesses, even after correcting for institutionalism and antipsychotic medication

original_title: Schizophrenia and smoking: an epidemiological survey in a state hospital
replication_title: Schizophrenia and tobacco smoking: a replication study in another US psychiatric hospital
description: Schizophrenia is associated with heavy smoking (more than 1.5 packs per day) among current smokers compared with other severe mental illnesses

original_title: Polydipsia and water intoxication in a long-term psychiatric hospital
replication_title: Polydipsia and schizophrenia in a psychiatric hospital: a replication study
description: Schizophrenia and smoking are independently associated with polydipsia in chronic psychiatric inpatients, after controlling for other factors including chronicity of hospitalization

original_title: Evidence for specific attention and working memory deficits in people with schizophrenia
replication_title: Neuropsychological evidence of a deficit in switching attention in schizophrenia-a replication study
description: Patients with schizophrenia exhibit specific deficits in switching attention and reloading of working memory tasks of the Visual Attention Battery (VAB), but are not impaired in control, selective, and divided attention conditions

original_title: Neuropsychological evidence for frontostriatal dysfunction in schizophrenia
replication_title: Neuropsychological evidence of a deficit in switching attention in schizophrenia-a replication study
description: Patients with schizophrenia are impaired on a set-shifting task of the CANTAB (Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery)

original_title: Thalamic volume reductions in schizophrenic patients
replication_title: Reversed planum temporale asymmetry in schizophrenia—A replication study
description: Thalamic volumes are significantly reduced in schizophrenic patients compared to control subjects

original_title: The association between HTR2C gene polymorphisms and the metabolic syndrome in patients with schizophrenia
replication_title: P.3.c.001 Association between HTR2C polymorphisms and the metabolic syndrome in patients using antipsychotics: a replication study
description: The variant rs1414334 C-allele of the HTR2C gene is associated with increased prevalence of the metabolic syndrome in patients with schizophrenia using antipsychotics

original_title: HTR2C gene polymorphisms and the metabolic syndrome in patients with schizophrenia: a replication study
replication_title: P.3.c.001 Association between HTR2C polymorphisms and the metabolic syndrome in patients using antipsychotics: a replication study
description: The variant rs1414334 C-allele of the HTR2C gene is associated with increased prevalence of the metabolic syndrome in patients with schizophrenia using antipsychotics

replication_title: Association of Superoxide Dismutase 2 (SOD2) Genotype with Gray Matter Volume Shrinkage in Chronic Alcohol Users: Replication and Further Evaluation of an Addiction Gene Panel

replication_title: Post-awakening Cortisol in Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technicians: A Replication Study in a Novel Population

replication_title: Is Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factor (Bdnf) Associated With Smoking Initiation? Replication Using a Large Finnish Population Sample
description: The BDNF Val66Met (rs6265) variant is associated with smoking initiation, with the major (Val) allele increasing risk of ever smoking (OR = 1.06 across 143,023 individuals)

original_title: Autism beyond diagnostic categories: characterization of autistic phenotypes in schizophrenia

original_title: Indicators of postpyloric feeding tube placement in children

original_title: An analysis of the relationship between job satisfaction and job stress in correctional nurses

original_title: Mortality risk attributable to high and low ambient temperature: a multicountry observational study

original_title: The evolving role of the healthcare CFO

original_title: Development of a mouse pain scale using sub-second behavioral mapping and statistical modeling

original_title: Genome-wide association studies of cerebral white matter lesion burden: the CHARGE consortium

original_title: A genome-wide association study identifies potential susceptibility loci for Hirschsprung disease
replication_title: Association Analysis of SLC6A20 Polymorphisms With Hirschsprung Disease
description: SLC6A20 polymorphisms are associated with susceptibility to Hirschsprung disease, as identified by a genome-wide association study

original_title: A comparison of the salary wage and hourly wage acute care nursing units. A pilot study

original_title: Clinical value of the Beery visual-motor integration supplemental tests of visual perception and motor coordination
replication_title: Clinical Value of the VMI Supplemental Tests: A Modified Replication Study

original_title: FoxP2 is significantly associated with schizophrenia and major depression in the Chinese Han population

original_title: Action anticipation through attribution of false belief by 2-year-olds

original_title: Where will the triangle look for it? Attributing false beliefs to a geometric shape at 17 months

original_title: On the selection of signals

original_title: Isolating exogenous and endogenous modes of temporal attention
